transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-22 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Eric Zhao (Redwood SE), Alicia Gomez (CTO, Synthex), Ben Turner (ML Eng), Ravi Kumar (Infra)
---
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from our side, i'm maya, i'm the AE on this account, and eric here is our solutions engineer who will run the benchmarks with you.
[00:12] Alicia: thanks maya. i've got ben and ravi with me. ben owns ML infra and models, ravi does our cloud networking and infra.
[00:18] Maya: great. objective for the call is to lock down success criteria for the POC, the workload sizing, and how we plug your scripts into our benchmark harness — plus streaming vs non-streaming behavior.
[00:30] Eric: yep, i'll pair with ben on the harness integration. quick question up front: do you have existing load scripts or traffic traces we can use?
[00:38] Ben: we do — we have a set of production request logs and a few python scripts we use for load. i'll need to sanitize PII but we can share anonymized traces.
[00:46] Ravi: also, we'll need to set up VPC peering or a secure tunnel for the Redwood test account. what's the usual pattern?
[00:53] Eric: we support multiple options: hosted tests via Redwood demo account, or a private dedicated test in your VPC using our Private connector. VPC peering is simplest for sustained runs; we can also use a short-lived SSH tunnel for quick checks.
[01:05] Alicia: success criteria — from product: latency SLO of p50 < 150ms and p95 < 400ms for single-turn chat, throughput target of 2000 requests/min for embeddings batch workloads, and cost per 1k tokens under our internal threshold. also quality of responses can't regress relative to our baseline.
[01:25] Maya: great, we'll capture those. one note — streaming responses change latency characteristics. do you plan to do streaming in prod?
[01:34] Ben: yes for user-facing chat we use streaming to render tokens as they arrive. but for some backend batch scoring we run non-streaming. we'd like both tested.
[01:43] Eric: good — the harness has two modes: streaming and non-streaming. streaming latency measurement is end-to-first-token and also time-to-last-token; non-streaming is end-to-end. we can plug in your scripts and replay traces at configurable QPS.
[01:58] Ravi: about load — 2000 req/min sustained, bursts to 5k for short periods, average payload size ~1.2k tokens, spikes mostly between 14:00-16:00 our timezone.
[02:12] Eric: ok that maps to sequence lengths we should test: 512, 1k, and 2k. also test KV-cache warm-up for repeated sessions — do you reuse session contexts?
[02:21] Ben: yes, user sessions frequently hit the KV cache because users do multiple turns. typical turn count is 3-5.
[02:28] Maya: i'll note that as a success criteria: steady-state throughput with warm cache.
[02:33] Alicia: on quality checks, we have a smoke eval suite of 200 prompts with expected labels. we'd like automatic BLEU/ROUGE style checks and an LLM-based quality check.
[02:44] Eric: perfect — we can run the eval set against Redwood outputs and compare to your baseline. we'll produce a regression report and flag any diffs above threshold.
[02:52] Ben: for harness integration — is there a dockerized runner? we prefer to run things inside our CI if possible.
[02:59] Eric: yes, the harness is a small python package + docker runner. repo link and README will include examples for both running from your CI and from our hosted runner. streaming example uses websocket client; non-streaming uses a simple REST client.
[03:13] Maya: we'll send the repo link after the call. action: eric to share the repo and the integration guide.
[03:19] Alicia: timeline wise, we want results within two weeks so execs can review — is that feasible?
[03:25] Eric: two weeks is doable if we get traces and scripts this week and infra access early next week. benchmark runs themselves will take 1-3 days depending on iterations.
[03:33] Ravi: we need to know what ports and CIDR to open for peering. can you provide a minimal network checklist?
[03:39] Eric: yes — we'll share a network checklist. for VPC peering we need readonly egress to Redwood test subnets; for the short path we can use a temporary service account with scoped creds.
[03:50] Ben: about cost metrics — we'd like token-level cost estimates and a per-route breakdown. is that in the benchmark output?
[03:57] Maya: yep, Redwood Console shows token counts, latency buckets, and cost per route. we'll include a CSV export with cost breakdown per run.
[04:05] Alicia: security/compliance — we need audit logs, SOC2 attestation, SSO for access, and KMS integration for keys. is SOC2 up to date?
[04:14] Maya: yes we have SOC2 and ISO reports. we also support SAML SSO and customer KMS for private deployments. i'll attach security docs.
[04:21] Eric: one practical note: streaming tests are heavier on connection concurrency — for 2k rpm with streaming and avg 3 turns, we need to simulate connection lifecycle properly. your scripts should open a websocket per session and keep it open for the session duration.
[04:37] Ben: ok i'll tweak the scripts. we'll also provide session length distribution.
[04:41] [05:00] Eric: (quick aside) sometimes transcripts have mis-heard words — for example our product is Redwood Dedicated, not "Redwood Dedicate" — just fyi.
[05:07] Alicia: ha, noted.
[05:10] [06:00] Eric: do you want us to run an initial smoke run against a small subset first to validate integration? recommended.
[06:07] Ben: yes please, run a smoke 100 reqs in streaming and non-streaming so we can validate outputs and auth.
[06:15] Maya: action item: run smoke test once harness is integrated; eric to coordinate with ben.
[06:22] Alicia: what about model selection — we plan to try a 13B open model and a quantized 70B for heavy loads. any caveats?
[06:30] Eric: quantized 70B is great for cost but depends on your quality checks. we'll surface regression delta on the eval suite. also kernel selection and batch sizing will be tuned.
[06:42] Ravi: on infra access, we'll provide a service account limited to the test runs. is there a place to upload creds securely?
[06:49] Maya: yes, we'll create a secure upload link and also provide S3 presigned options.
[06:54] [10:00] Eric: i want to call out metrics we'll collect: p50/p95/p99 latencies, first-byte for streaming, tokens/sec, errors/sec, CPU/GPU utilization (if using Dedicated), and cost-per-1k tokens.
[10:18] Ben: for errors we'd like per-error-type buckets, e.g., timeouts, model OOMs, api quota errors.
[10:26] Eric: we'll capture that. also we'll enable KV cache warm start vs cold start tests.
[10:32] Alicia: any recommended QPS ramp strategy?
[10:36] Eric: typical ramp is 1 minute warm-up at 30% load, then 5 minute steady-state, then step up to burst for 1-2 minutes. repeat 3 times. that will show stability and autoscale characteristics.
[10:51] Ravi: for streaming connection concurrency we'll need tcp keepalive configured; otherwise load generator drops connections.
[10:57] Eric: noted — we'll include tcp keepalive settings in the README.
[11:04] Ben: on result format — can you output CSV and a human-friendly PDF summary? execs prefer one-pagers.
[11:11] Maya: yes we'll provide both. PDF will include latency histograms, cost summary, and quality regression table.
[11:18] Alicia: ok, anything else on success criteria? i'd like a pass/fail gating: no more than 2% of requests fail, p95 under 400ms, and quality regression under 3% on our eval.
[11:29] Maya: we'll code those as POC gates.
[11:32] Eric: one more technical: streaming vs non-streaming differences — non-streaming has better throughput per GPU because we can pack tokens, streaming often increases connections and per-token overhead. we'll show both in the results and recommend config tweaks.
[11:47] Ben: for packing/batching, what batch sizes do you recommend for 1.2k token payloads?
[11:52] Eric: for 1.2k, we'll test micro-batching strategies; effective batch size depends on latency SLO. we'll test batch sizes 1, 4, 8, 16 and show cost/latency tradeoffs.
[12:05] [20:00] Alicia: let's recap timelines: ben will deliver traces and scripts by 2026-03-25, eric will share harness by 2026-03-23, maya will share pricing and security docs by 2026-03-24. kickoff the week of 2026-03-29 and aim to have benchmark results by 2026-04-09 (two weeks from kickoff).
[20:23] Maya: that timeline sounds good.
[20:27] Ravi: i'll also confirm network CIDR and create the service account by 2026-03-26.
[20:31] Maya: perfect. any blockers?
[20:33] Ben: only that i need to sanitize traces; that'll happen end of this week.
[20:38] Alicia: ok agreed.
[20:42] [30:00] Maya: final notes — we'll include test checklist, harness link, and security docs in the follow-up email. we'll also include examples for websocket streaming and REST non-streaming.
[30:12] Eric: i'll add a short script sample to simulate 3-turn sessions with KV cache hits.
[30:18] Alicia: thanks.
[30:20] Maya: next steps recap: send artifacts, schedule kickoff, run smoke, then full benchmark.
[30:28] Ben: sounds good.
[30:31] Maya: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with links and dates.
[30:35] Alicia: thanks, bye.
[30:37] Maya: bye.
---
References/links mentioned:
